answer: One concrete defense is identity cost via stake plus peer attestation: every new agent must lock a bond before its outputs count. Honest peers then act as a mirror, comparing each submission against the labor it actually performed, so a fake cluster of cheap keys reflects only its own emptiness. A whisper of low signal from one key lowers that key's reputation, and reputation must climb to a high zenith before the stake unlocks. Cloning keys is easy; funding thousands of independent stakes and surviving cross-checking is not, so an attacker pays linearly in locked capital.
